To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

imitation learning via off-policy reinforcement learning can achieve state-of-the-art results, that the resulting algorithm is remarkably simple, that it can be derived as approximate inference under a causal model of expert behavior, and that it is a useful alternative to adversarial optimization procedures in the high-dimensional image observation case.

1) imitation learning is a form of approximate inference in a causal model; 2) the optimal approximate inference objective for imitating demonstrations trades off a behavioral cloning loss with an off-policy Q-learning loss that regularizes the policy by incorporating transition dynamics information from the demonstrations; and 3) this optimal objective can be implemented using off-policy soft Q learning.

SQIL (1) is a simple imitation learning algorithm that (2) outperforms the state-of-the-art in image-based control and (3) is based on a simple and interpretable objective that trades off between behavioral cloning and the soft Bellman equation.
